chunks: Not one of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I wrote to him asking him about a man upon whom is the dower of his wife, which she does not seek from him, either out of kindness to her husband or out of shyness. He wrote: Zakat is not obligatory upon him except in his wealth.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on a husband's unpaid dowry debt before he pays it to his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that Zakat on a deferred dower (Mahr) is not obligatory on the debt itself until the husband actually possesses the wealth to pay it, distinguishing between the liability and the actualized asset. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle that Zakat is levied on tangible, possessed wealth rather than mere obligations, addressing cases where a husband delays payment out of affection or modesty. It underscores the practical implication that the wife’s claim does not trigger Zakat on the husband’s side until the funds are in his possession and meet the nisab threshold.

en.hubeali: Someone else from our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘I wrote to himasws asking himasws about a man upon whom is a dower of his wife, she not seeking it from him, either from kindness with her husband, or from embarrassment. So it remains like that upon the man for his life and her life. Would the Zakāt be Obligated upon that dower or not?’ So heasws wrote: ‘The Zakāt would not be Obligated upon him except with regards to his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 11. More than one person of our people has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has said the following: “I once wrote to him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who owes Mahr of his woman who does not ask for payment due to sympathy or shyness. It goes on for their lifetime. Is he required to pay Zakat for that Mahr?
He (the Imam) wrote, ‘Zakat is not due on him except for his assets.’”
